sections.h2: How large is Volusia County, and who lives in its houses?
sections.html:
Land area in Volusia County is 1,101.31 square miles. The 2020 census found 553,543 people, against 494,593 ten years earlier, and the mid-2025 estimate of 606,573 sits 9.6 percent above the 2020 base. Age stands out: 27.3 percent of the population has passed 65, and 46,354 residents are veterans.

Across 241,881 households for 2020 to 2024, owners live in 73.7 percent of homes. The midpoint owner home is valued at $313,000 and gross rent at the midpoint is $1,467. Builders pulled 2,826 permits in 2025. Those figures come from Census QuickFacts. With so many older owners and veterans, the exemption categories further down are worth reading before any sale.

sections.h2: How does a Volusia County parcel travel from value to bill?
sections.html:
Three hand-offs turn a parcel into a bill. The property appraiser sets value and decides exemptions, and the county council, school board, city commissions and other levying bodies choose millage. A mill is one dollar of tax on each thousand dollars of taxable value.

Once the appraiser finishes the roll and the Department of Revenue approves it, the appraiser certifies it to the tax collector, who mails each notice to the owner's last address of record. The collector also describes ad valorem tax as paid in arrears, because the year runs January 1 to December 31 and the bill arrives after it ends. You get one bill per parcel, following how the deed was recorded. The appraiser mails a Notice of Proposed Taxes in August, listing value and hearing dates.

sections.h2: What should a Volusia County owner do when a bill never arrives?
sections.html:
Ask for it. Section 197.122 puts three duties on the owner: know that tax is due each year, find out the amount, and pay before delinquency. A lost envelope is no defense.

The collector mails annual bills on or before November 1 and asks owners to call if nothing has come by the second week of the month. Installment participants get quarterly statements in June, September, December and March instead. A parcel whose taxes run through a lender escrow gets an informational notice saying the original went to the escrow trustee. After a move or a sale, update the mailing address on the appraiser's records, which the collector says the appraiser maintains along with the legal description.

sections.h2: Which dates frame the Volusia County tax year?
sections.html:
The collector's own pages supply the calendar below. A deadline falling on a weekend or holiday moves a working day later for walk-in payments before 5 p.m. and online payments before 11:59 p.m. Eastern.

Volusia County collector calendar
DateEvent
On or about Nov. 1Bills mailed
March 31Last penalty-free day, and the cutoff for a deferral application
April 1Delinquent, with a 3 percent minimum charge
April 30Advertising deadline and last day to apply for a new installment plan
Last business day of May, 4:30 p.m.Cutoff to pay in an office and avoid a certificate

Source: Volusia County Tax Collector, important dates. The 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent discounts run November through February; March carries none. A payment postmarked after April 1 is priced by the day the office receives it.

sections.h2: How do installment payments work in Volusia County?
sections.html:
The plan is open to owners whose estimated tax tops $100, with the estimate taken from last year's gross tax. The Form DR-534 is available November 1 through April 30 and must reach the office at 123 W. Indiana Ave., Room 103, DeLand, before May 1.

Four quarterly statements follow. June and September amounts rest on the prior year's tax, and any change from new value or exemptions is trued up in December and March once the roll is certified. If the first payment is made by June 30, the owner does not reapply next year. Call the office if the first notice has not arrived by June 15. Anything still unpaid on April 1 is handled as a delinquent real estate tax. Mortgage borrowers should not enroll, since lenders must pay in November to earn the maximum discount.

sections.h2: Can a Volusia County owner make a partial payment?
sections.html:
Yes, before April 1, on real and business property, with a sworn affidavit mailed along with the check. A partial payment is anything below the full amount due.

  • Installment accounts cannot use it.
  • No discount applies once an agreement with the collector exists.
  • Whatever remains unpaid on April 1 becomes delinquent and is due in full.
  • Taxes not paid in full at an office by 4:30 p.m. on the last business day of May lead to a certificate on the parcel.

sections.h2: How does a tax certificate sale run in Volusia County?
sections.html:
The sale is held online through LienHub by June 1, and certificate information posts there in mid-May. Before it, a list of delinquent parcels is advertised once a week for three weeks, starting at the north end of the county and working south in parcel order. The paper lists more parcels than will sell, because payments arrive after the list is built.

Cost to a buyer covers the gross tax, a 3 percent fee, advertising and sale costs. A winning bid cannot exceed 18 percent simple interest and pays at least 5 percent unless bid at zero. Interest begins accruing the month after issue. A parcel with no bidder goes to the county at 18 percent.

To clear the lien, an owner pays the certificate amount plus the sold rate through the redemption month, and a $6.25 fee applies from June 1. The collector takes cash, a cashier's or certified check, a money order or a card. A certificate lasts seven years and can be sold between investors for a $2.25 recording fee. Buyers may not contact owners about payment until two years after April 1 of the issue year, and a buyer who does can be barred from the sale.

sections.h2: What must a certificate holder do before Volusia County sets a tax deed sale?
sections.html:
After two years, a holder who wants a deed applies through LienHub, and one certificate is enough. The collector's example counts from taxes that went delinquent April 1, 2021, which allowed an application after April 1, 2023.

The applicant first pays the redemption amounts on all other certificates, any omitted or delinquent taxes, current taxes if due, and statutory fees including an application fee and a title search fee. The Clerk of the Circuit Court administers the auction itself, and the collector refers questions there. A homeowner who spots a certificate on the parcel can still redeem it with the collector before a sale takes place.

sections.h2: Which exemption categories does the Volusia County appraiser list?
sections.html:
The appraiser's exemption page names twelve groupings and gives the records department's number, 386-736-5901, for questions.

  • Homestead, senior, disability, veteran, and widow or widower.
  • Granny flat and first responder.
  • Religious, literary, charitable and educational property.
  • Conservation, economic development and historical.
  • Agricultural classification.

Homestead is the largest. State guidance puts it at up to $50,000, with $25,000 reaching every levy and a second slice on assessed value over $50,000 that skips school taxes. Filing closes March 1, and the home must be a permanent residence on January 1, per the state homestead guide. The benefit belongs to one owner. After a sale, the home returns to market value the next January 1.

sections.h2: What should a Volusia County seller settle before closing?
sections.html:
Put the payoff in writing from the tax collector, with a figure good through closing. Because the year is paid in arrears, a closing in July leaves half the year's tax unbilled, and the contract decides who covers it.

Check the parcel's balance and any certificate on the collector's search first. Deed stamps cost seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price, per the Department of Revenue, and the contract should name who pays. If a tax deed application may exist on a certificate older than two years, ask the clerk as well.

faqs.q: Until what day can Volusia owners pay with no penalty?
faqs.a: March 31. Weekend or holiday deadlines roll forward for in person and online payments, but the 3 percent charge starts April 1.

faqs.q: Is there a Volusia County discount if I pay in December?
faqs.a: Yes, 3 percent. November pays 4 percent, January 2 percent, February 1 percent and March none.

faqs.q: Can I redeem a certificate on my Volusia County home by card?
faqs.a: Yes. The collector takes cash, cashier's or certified checks, money orders and credit or debit cards, and the owner owes the rate bid at the sale.

faqs.q: How soon can a Volusia County certificate become a deed application?
faqs.a: After two years, counted from April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. The holder applies through LienHub.

faqs.q: Who should I call in Volusia County about exemptions?
faqs.a: The property appraiser's records department at 386-736-5901. The collector handles bills, installments and deferral filings.
